final_answer:
All done. Here's what was implemented:

**`ringbuf.c`** — Ring buffer with opaque struct, using `head`/`tail`/`count` pointers on a `uint8_t[]` backing store:

| Function | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `rb_create(cap)` | Allocates buffer with `capacity - 1` usable slots (reserved slot distinguishes full from empty) |
| `rb_destroy(rb)` | Frees buffer; safely handles `NULL` |
| `rb_write(rb, data, len)` | Writes up to `len` bytes, writes what fits if ring is full, returns actual count written |
| `rb_read(rb, out, len)` | Reads oldest-first up to `len` bytes, returns actual count read |
| `rb_peek()` | Copy-read without advancing tail |
| `rb_size()` / `rb_capacity()` | Query filled count and allocated capacity |
| `rb_clear()` | Resets head/tail/count without freeing storage |

- Wrap-around handled via modulo arithmetic in both paths (single-block copy when no wrap needed, two-block copy when wrapping)
- Compiled cleanly with `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror` — all tests passed
